Hello people of Sol! I've reset usage limits for all ChatGPT Work and Codex users. Together with that, a quick update on GPT-5.6 Sol usage limits.

Over the past few weeks, many of you have told us that Sol was using your Codex limits faster than expected. To be clear, we have not reduced usage on any subscription plans.

We’ve been digging into what was happening and have landed several improvements. As a result, we expect your usage to last around 18% longer during typical use of Sol. Some of you should already see significantly larger improvements from today. Tomorrow, we’ll also restore the five-hour limit that we temporarily paused while investigating.

Here’s what we found:
- GPT-5.6 Sol is much more willing to work for longer, make additional tool calls, and coordinate complex workflows across tools and subagents. That makes it better at solving hard problems, but some tasks were using far more than we intended.
- Sol also works harder at the same reasoning effort than previous models. High on Sol can use more tokens than High did on GPT-5.5.
- Programmatic tool calling, also referred to as code mode, gives Sol much more flexibility to run tool calls in parallel or continue working while waiting. But it also led to more responses per turn, more cached input tokens, and higher usage than expected.
- This was particularly noticeable when Sol was waiting for tool calls to finish or running many web searches. We’ve improved how we handle both cases and are continuing to make code mode more efficient.
- The impact was also very uneven. The median user actually found Sol quite token efficient, while some power users working on harder tasks saw their usage drain much faster. We were very focused on average and median usage before launch and missed some cases where the long tail could use significantly more usage.

Sol is a significant step forward in what Codex can do, but capability and efficiency do not always improve at the same pace, and some issues only become clear once people are using the model at real-world scale. We should have recognized this sooner and been more upfront about it.

You keep pushing the frontier and we’ll keep improving efficiency and sharing updates as we go.

The negative AI jobs outcome just continues to not be happening as some predicted. A large portion of enterprises I talk with -across industries- are still hiring, just with a tilt in the kind of roles they’re going after.

They’re finding that AI is letting them do more, and Jevons paradox is actually playing out. They’re hiring engineers to go after problems they couldn’t tackle before. They’re hiring in sales because they can go deeper in client relationships now with the help of AI. They’re hiring in internal FDEs to help them deploy AI. And so on.

Anyone using AI merely to cut costs eventually just gets outcompeted by companies that use AI to better serve their customers and drive more breakthroughs in their business. 

Could this trend change at some point? Sure. But for now this appears to be the trajectory we’re on.

tweets.text:
There’s still so much opportunity in the diffusion of AI into the real world. Most enterprises are going to need a ton of support to be able to apply the model breakthroughs to their workflows.

Intelligence alone is not enough to transform most processes because you need to bridge that intelligence with real world feedback loops. That requires connecting to various enterprise systems, getting the right data to the AI, enabling humans to make decisions at different steps in a process through the right UX, having workflows that improve the underlying data and models over time, dealing with regulatory and compliance challenges, and more. 

The way you implement AI agents for doing client onboarding in a bank is entirely different from contract review in a legal team. In life sciences, financial services, legal, manufacturing, and many other critical industries, AI is only valuable if it makes contact with the real world in a contextual way. 

The way that interaction is going to happen is through an applied AI layer. Some of that will come from the labs directly, but lots of the opportunity will necessarily come from independent companies that can go deep in each industry.

And counter to some beliefs, this need isn’t reduced even as AI model capability improves over time. In fact, the better the models get, the more ambitious you can be in the workflows you can automate, which generally requires even more of this applied layer. Tons of opportunity right now.
tweets.summary_zh: 现实世界中将 AI 技术应用到企业还面临很多机会和挑战。虽然 AI 本身很智能，但要使其真正有效，还需要与实际工作流程结合，获取合适的数据，解决合规问题等。不同的行业在使用 AI 的方法上也各有不同，所以目前仍有大量机会可以探索。

tweets.text:
Claude Opus 5 is out now, and it's a huge jump over Opus 4.8 on a wide number of capabilities. 

At Box, we've been testing Claude Opus 5 with the Box AI Agent on Box's Complex Work Eval, our agentic benchmark that puts models through real enterprise document work end-to-end across a variety of industries.  We saw meaningful gains in performance across some of the most complex enterprise tasks on unstructured data. 

Here are a few examples of some of the wins we saw in testing:

* Due diligence (+17%): On a transaction due-diligence review, Opus 5 worked through the full set of required findings and flagged the ones Opus 4.8 missed. It stays thorough as the checklist grows instead of catching the obvious items and stopping.

* Life Sciences (+30%): On a target-identification task, it intersected several ranked datasets under a strict matching rule to find the targets common to all of them. Opus 4.8 over-included partial matches and dropped genuine ones.

* Legal (+12%): On a clause-by-clause contract review against a policy, Opus 5 scored every item and correctly cleared the clauses that were acceptable under an exception where Opus 4.8 both missed items and mis-scored the exception.

* Technology (+19%) and Healthcare (+13%) showed the same pattern: complete, precise, multi-step analysis over messy source material.

Overall, the reasoning, analytical, and data processing skills of Opus 5 outshine Opus 4.8 meaningfully. Going to be very powerful for enterprise agentic use-cases. You'll be able to build agents with Opus 5 in the Box AI Studio shortly.

tweets.text:
Very happy to have Box sign this letter. We’re big believers in the power of open weights AI.

Open weights models help to drive the industry forward in a variety of ways to ensure more innovation, creativity, and diffusion of AI.

You get to have layers of the stack that emerge to post train models for highly specific purposes, which makes AI more useful in real world scenarios. Instead of waiting for just a few players to go deep in a domain, you get dozens or hundreds of attempts at that vertical, like in finance, life sciences, legal, healthcare, and more.

You get to see variance in how to handle safety and cyber risks. Instead of just one approach, you get a peek into what happens advanced capabilities can be used to build better systems to are used to defend systems. 

You get alternative approaches to training and building AI models. In more compute constrained environments, you develop more novel and efficient approaches to model training, which every other lab can learn from. 

And you get different cost structures for different workloads. High end and orchestration tasks can go to the closed frontier models and specific workhorse tasks can be done more cheaply. 

Open vs. closed is not a zero sum battle. The reason why you want strong open weights models is because it pushes the entire AI industry forward.
tweets.summary_zh:
很高兴看到Box（我们公司）签署了这封信。我们坚信“开放权重AI”的力量。

开放权重模型（允许大家自由使用和修改的AI模型）让整个行业更加创新和多样化。这样一来，各个行业（比如金融、医疗等）都有很多公司可以尝试不同的解决方案，而不是让少数公司主导一切。

它还能让我们看到处理安全和网络风险的多种方法，不同的公司会有不同的做法，这样我们就能找到更好的系统防御方案。

此外，开放模型还能让人们在有限的计算资源环境下，发明更高效的训练方法，让各个实验室都能受益。

tweets.text:
BREAKING: Claude Opus 5 is OUT NOW!

And…it’s a hard model to love.

We’ve spent the last week @every testing it across coding, writing, knowledge work, and our internal agent.

It argued with instructions, stopped before the work was finished, and generally didn’t play well with our existing skills and plugins like Compound Engineering. Our first reaction was: What have they done to my boy?

Then we deleted our existing skills and started from scratch.

Without the elaborate workflows we had built for earlier models, Opus 5 got dramatically better, and even showed flashes of brilliance.

Here’s our Day 0 vibe check:

- It’s a poor man’s Fable. It has many of Fable’s personality quirks without Fable’s genius.
- It breaks backward compatibility. If you’re using it with existing skills and workflows, watch out. It will often stop early or otherwise miss your instructions.
- If you start from scratch, you’ll have better results. @KieranKlaassen figured out that if he just started from scratch without his existing skills, he could get dramatically better results. This is a model that takes some time to rebuild your workflows around—but if you do, there’s a payoff waiting.
- Medium or low effort works better. @KieranKlassenn also found better results using Opus 5 on lower thinking levels. It seems that the more time you give it to think, the more likely it is to do the more annoying behaviors. Don’t just switch to Sonnet for a faster response! Try low thinking.

I have two slots in my workflow:

1. The genius model I use for my biggest hardest tasks, currently Fable.
2. The smart, fast generalist I use for everything else, currently GPT-5.6.

Opus 5 has the personality of the genius, but doesn’t have its top end. So that puts it in a strange middle ground that doesn’t really have a home in my day to day. I think I’ll use it mostly when I run out of Fable tokens.

full vibe check on @every in the next tweet 👇

How do you manage security for effectively infinite agents when identity and access management was designed for a finite number of employees?

Traditionally, each employee has an identity, a role, permissions, and a lifecycle.

tweets.text:
Very good post from the Head of Economics at Anthropic. They’re finding that jobs have been less negatively impacted by AI than expected, as we continue to see time and time again in the data.

The reason for this is that AI - at least so far - still requires people to operate to produce value in most cases. Most jobs can’t be fully automated with AI, only certain tasks in those jobs. And when you automate specific tasks, you actually can get even more output from those jobs, raising the demand (or at least maintaining it) in many cases.

“So far, AI is both skill-biased and labor-augmenting. It complements domain expertise. It relies on humans in the loop to direct and evaluate the most complex work. And it rewards AI proficiency. Model capabilities are improving fast, but remain stubbornly jagged. To fill in the pockets of the jagged frontier, expert oversight is needed to steer incredibly capable AI systems, and to recover when they falter.”

I suspect that we continue to see this in a number of critical areas of work. It’s clearly happening in software engineering, where software produced is being multiplied, all of which still requires developers to manage the work agents are doing. Software engineers are needed in a wide variety of industries now and companies of all sizes can now light up software projects that would have been impractical before.

But there will be plenty of other domains of work where demand remains strong in a world where agents can accelerate the output of that job. Jevons paradox is alive and well.
tweets.summary_zh: 这篇文章提到，AI 对工作的影响没有想象中那么大。虽然AI技术在不断进步，但大部分工作还是需要人来操作，AI只能帮助完成一些任务，而无法完全取代人类。因此，AI实际上可能会让工作效率更高，从而增加对某些职位的需求。比如，在软件工程领域，虽然AI能提高生产力，开发者仍然是必不可少的。而且，随着AI的应用，其他行业的工作需求也会继续保持强劲。

tweets.text:
So much of conversation is on company Strategy…but Culture always eats strategy for breakfast.

So what does Culture for startups mean? How does it get created? Where does it come from?

Startup culture stems from 3 areas:
—> The founder’s personality and DNA
—> The early team’s personality and DNA
—> The early products personality and DNA

A lot of these overlap and reinforce each other.

Some of it is top down….some of it is emergent.

It sucks when the emergence is artificially dampened..because perhaps the founder is too weak to instittuionalize.

It also sucks when there is so much difference of opinion that you end up getting pockets of different culture.

I don’t want to get dragged into DEI nonsense. We can be from different backgrounds but all agree to be part of the same company culture.
tweets.summary_zh:
很多人谈论公司的战略，但文化往往更重要，甚至能影响战略的实施。创业公司的文化来自创始人的性格、早期团队的特质和早期产品的特点，这些因素相互交织在一起。

如果创始人无法有效建立文化，或者团队之间出现太多意见分歧，就会造成不和谐的文化环境。不过，大家背景不同也没关系，只要都能认同公司的文化就好。

producthunt.summary_zh: Context.dev 是一个API工具，能够从互联网上抓取、丰富和提取数据。用户可以通过它轻松获取网站上的信息，并将这些数据进行整理和分析。它适用于各种数据集成和自动化需求。

producthunt.name: AnySearch
producthunt.tagline: Real-time structured search trusted by agents and developers
producthunt.summary_zh: AnySearch是一款实时的结构化搜索工具，专为代理和开发者设计。它能快速整理和提供准确的信息，让用户能够高效地找到所需的数据和答案。通过直观的界面，AnySearch简化了搜索过程，提高了工作效率。

producthunt.name: Fuzzy AI
producthunt.tagline: We warm your prospects before reaching out
producthunt.summary_zh: Fuzzy AI 是一款智能营销工具，旨在通过人工智能技术分析潜在客户的兴趣和行为。在你联系他们之前，Fuzzy AI 可以自动为你预热这些客户，提高成交的可能性。它让营销更加高效，节省时间和精力。

producthunt.name: Glaze by Raycast
producthunt.tagline: Create your own Mac apps by chatting with AI
producthunt.summary_zh: Glaze by Raycast 是一款让用户通过与人工智能对话来创建自己的 Mac 应用程序的工具。用户只需简单输入想法，AI 就能快速生成应用的代码和功能，让开发变得更加轻松。这个产品降低了编程门槛，适合任何想要自定义应用的人。

producthunt.name: Sim
producthunt.tagline: Open-source workspace for AI agents and workflows
producthunt.summary_zh: Sim 是一个开源的平台，专为人工智能代理和工作流程设计。用户可以在这个平台上创建、管理和协作各种 AI 任务，提高工作效率。它支持自定义和扩展，适合不同的工作需求。

producthunt.name: Fypro
producthunt.tagline: Convert your TikTok followers into paying customers
producthunt.summary_zh: Fypro 是一款工具，可以帮助用户将 TikTok 上的粉丝转化为付费客户。它提供数据分析和营销功能，使用户能够有效地推广产品和服务，从而实现收益增长。

producthunt.name: Unabyss for Claude
producthunt.tagline: Shared memory across all apps and LLMs. In Claude
producthunt.summary_zh: Unabyss for Claude是一个用在Claude平台上的工具，它允许用户在多个应用和大型语言模型（LLMs）之间共享记忆。通过这个产品，用户可以更高效地保存和访问信息，实现跨应用的数据同步。

producthunt.name: Cursor for iOS
producthunt.tagline: Build with coding agents from anywhere
producthunt.summary_zh: Cursor for iOS 是一款移动应用，允许用户通过编程代理在任何地方编写和管理代码。它提供了一个直观的界面，方便用户进行代码编辑、调试和项目管理。无论你是新手还是有经验的开发者，都可以在此平台上轻松工作。

producthunt.name: ExploreYC
producthunt.tagline: Open-source API for Y Combinator & a16z company data
producthunt.summary_zh: ExploreYC 是一个开源API，提供Y Combinator和a16z公司的数据。用户可以通过这个API获取相关公司的信息、融资情况和其他关键数据，方便进行研究和分析。

producthunt.name: Velo 3.0
producthunt.tagline: AI video infrastructure to explain, train, and sell faster.
producthunt.summary_zh: Velo 3.0 是一个基于人工智能的视频基础设施。它可以快速创建视频内容，用于说明产品、进行培训和销售，从而提升信息传递的效率。通过智能化的方式，用户可以更轻松地制作专业视频。

producthunt.name: Lev8
producthunt.tagline: Find, research, and reach the right people
producthunt.summary_zh: Lev8是一款帮助用户寻找和联系合适人选的工具。它允许用户进行深入的研究，以便更好地了解目标群体并与之建立联系。通过Lev8，用户可以简化信息获取和沟通的过程。

producthunt.name: Prefactor
producthunt.tagline: Evaluate your AI Agents in real-time
producthunt.summary_zh: Prefactor是一个实时评估AI代理的工具。它能够帮助用户监测和分析AI代理的表现，让用户更好地理解其工作效果。通过这个工具，用户可以即时获取反馈，优化AI代理的使用。

github_trending.description: A lightweight, cloud-native GIS platform for visualizing, exploring, and analyzing geospatial data. It runs in the web browser, on the desktop, on mobile, and inside Jupyter notebooks.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个轻量级的地理信息系统平台，可以帮助用户在浏览器、桌面和手机上可视化、探索和分析地理数据。对于Yves来说，它可能对Logic Labs（AI公司）更有帮助，因为这个平台可以应用于地理数据分析，支持与AI相关的创意项目和研究。同时，这种工具也能助力于提升品牌营销策略，尤其是在地理定位方面。

github_trending.description: 💖🧸 Self hosted, you-owned Grok Companion, a container of souls of waifu, cyber livings to bring them into our worlds, wishing to achieve Neuro-sama's altitude. Capable of realtime voice chat, Minecraft, Factorio playing. Web / macOS / Windows supported.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个自托管的虚拟助手，可以进行实时语音聊天并在游戏中互动，类似于拥有一个数字角色伙伴。对于Yves来说，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI公司）更具价值，因为它展示了如何将人工智能应用于互动体验，能为创意设计提供新的灵感和方向，同时也可以探索在电商环境中虚拟角色的潜力。

github_trending.description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个智能代理系统，旨在优化性能，通过技能、记忆和安全机制来提升代码生成和开发效率，适用于多种代码生成工具。对Yves来说，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI公司）最有帮助，因为它可以提升AI模型的开发效率，帮助公司更好地进行产品研发，同时也能激发他在创意设计方面的想法。

github_trending.description: Build local voice agents with open-source models
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目旨在构建本地语音代理，允许用户通过开源模型进行语音识别与合成，从而实现人机对话。对Yves来说，这个项目对Logic Labs（AI公司）特别有帮助，因为它可以用于开发更智能的语音助手，提升AI产品的交互体验，同时也能为TexTale的电商平台提供个性化的客户服务，增强用户体验。作为创意设计从业者，他可以利用这个工具来探索创意的语音交互设计，激发新的设计灵感。
这个项目是用 Rust 编写的高效内存管理工具，主要用于提升计算机程序在处理数据时的性能和资源利用率。对于Yves而言，这个项目可以支持Logic Labs在开发AI应用时优化系统性能，从而提高AI模型的处理能力和运行效率，同时也能为TexTale的电商平台提供更流畅的用户体验。作为一名创意设计从业者，他可以借助这个项目的技术背景，探索在设计中如何利用高效的内存管理来提升创意工具的性能。

github_trending.description: A free open source IT asset/license management system
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个免费的开源IT资产和许可证管理系统，帮助企业管理它们的硬件和软件资源。对于Yves而言，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI公司）更有帮助，因为它可以有效管理公司的IT资产，提升运营效率，释放更多时间用于AI创新和设计。同时，对于TexTale（科技服装电商），良好的IT管理也可以确保其电商平台的稳定性与安全性。
这个项目是一个深度伪造软件，允许用户用人工智能技术把一个人的脸替换成另一个人的脸，广泛应用于视频和图像处理。对于Yves来说，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI 公司）更有价值，因为它展示了如何运用AI技术进行创意设计，同时也为电商品牌营销提供了创新的视觉内容创作方式。
这个项目是一个开源的语音人工智能工具，旨在帮助开发者创建更自然和灵活的语音交互体验。对于Yves来说，VibeVoice可以为Logic Labs的AI产品开发提供强大的技术支持，同时在TexTale的电商平台中提升用户与产品的互动体验，有助于实现更具吸引力的品牌营销。作为创意设计从业者，VibeVoice也为他提供了丰富的创意设计灵感和工具，帮助他在语音交互设计方面展开更多创意探索。

github_trending.description: The open-source alternative to Claude Cowork (powered by opencode)
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个开源的平台，旨在为用户提供一个协作的工作环境，利用AI技术提升团队合作的效率。对于Yves来说，这个工具可以帮助Logic Labs提升AI相关项目的协作效果，同时也可以为TexTale提供数据驱动的创意设计支持，提升电商运营的灵活性和创意性。

github_trending.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个技能框架和软件开发方法论，帮助团队更有效地进行协作和开发工作，用于提升项目执行的能力。对于Yves来说，这个项目可以在Logic Labs（AI公司）中提供管理和开发方面的指导，帮助他更好地利用AI工具进行创新设计，同时提高团队的协作效率。
